digest.component_or_area: git-backed tickets store compaction and sync recovery
propositions: Parallel multi-session writes to the tickets store cause wedging when compaction mutates the worktree before git commit, leaving dirty artifacts if the worker dies and blocking sync/push operations.

Tracked runtime markers (*/.archived, */.write.lock) committed before gitignore patterns existed are never un-tracked, causing routine marker churn to appear as dirty tree in git status checks and stranding local ticket commits.

Compaction fold and sync reconverge operations do not atomically handle two failure modes: untracked files that origin wants to create, and tracked file deletions/modifications that would be overwritten by merge.
Store-wide scans (fsck, compact-all) must traverse the entire ticket directory including archived tickets, causing scalability issues as archived content grows.
fsck and doctor commands lack detection and repair for dirty-tree, stale-lock, and orphaned marker classes left by interrupted compaction folds.
Push operations do not recover from the same untracked-collision and tracked-deletion abort classes that affect sync reconverge.
